Given the CRITICAL severity, a SECOND independent Agent review (not self-verification) was run specifically on the repair -- confirmed the tuple fix is fully, genuinely correct (independently constructed namedtuple/50k-deep-tuple/3-way-mixed-nesting cases beyond the implementer's own tests), and found one new WARNING (a self-referential structure hangs forever) plus minor items, repaired in 8452b94. That repair's own first attempt (a total-visited-node cap) was caught failing this session's own regression run (not by any reviewer) -- it silently reintroduced a many-minutes-long hang for a legitimate input class before finally raising, AND separately broke a genuine large notebook fixture in test_obligation_cell_editor.py. Root-caused to depth vs. node-count and fixed properly (depth-bounded, not node-count-bounded) in the same commit, per this project's own "after two unsuccessful repair attempts, return to first principles" rule. This is the most heavily adversarially-tested taskcard in this engagement so far -- 2 separate G2 reviews plus one self-caught regression, none of which were rubber stamps.

tasks.title: Atomic write loses permissions, no fsync, undecided symlink policy
tasks.objective: Preserve destination mode, fsync, write-through-symlink policy.
tasks.note: Implementation 6b08f13; independent Taskcard-Gate-G2 review (separate Agent, using WSL/Ubuntu to genuinely exercise real POSIX chmod/symlink/fsync semantics unavailable on this Windows dev machine) found 0 CRITICAL, 5 issues (verdict ISSUES_FOUND) -- most notably a real symlink-loop bug: Path.resolve() on CPython 3.11/3.12 raises RuntimeError (not OSError) for a symlink loop, leaking past the NotebookWriteError contract, undetectable from Windows alone since the same input behaves differently there. Repaired in 022b12c, independently re-verified for real on WSL/Ubuntu (18/18 checks pass, including the fixed loop behavior). This taskcard is notable for using WSL as a genuine second-platform verification tool, not just code reading/reasoning or mocks -- recommended precedent for any future taskcard with platform-divergent behavior.
